This is the LESSONS P9 Pareto-frontier path: the trust gate is non-negotiable, but the quality lift is real.

test, narrower than the future Iter 4 mb-qxrm "full Wave 5 live-fire
matrix". This bead validates JUST the Iter 3 mobile-inbox -> desktop
transcript happy path.

Requires the iOS Shortcut to be installed per
docs/mobile/ios-shortcut.md INCLUDING the Open App: Obsidian action
(Action 3, per Wave 0 Finding 5).

Smoke sequence:
1. Confirm Mockingbird desktop running, MobileSyncEnabled ON,
   VaultPath set, build is current with Iter 3 implementation
   (Waves 3.1 + 3.2 + 3.3 landed).
2. Install or update the Shortcut on iPhone per the setup doc
   (3-action shape: Record Audio + Save File + Open App: Obsidian).
3. Trigger the Shortcut (back-tap, icon, or Action Button).
4. Record a short voice memo (5-10 sec).
5. Confirm save destination in the Files picker -> inbox/.
6. Shortcut's Action 3 foregrounds Obsidian Mobile.
7. Within ~30-60 s: file syncs to desktop's <vault>/inbox/, watcher
   picks it up, courier processes through full pipeline.
8. Verify on desktop:
   - New row appears in Dictations page with source='mobile-inbox',
     start_mode='in_app' (or whatever the courier-ingest mode label
     resolves to per Iter 1).
   - Cleaned transcript is non-empty and matches what was spoken.
   - File moved from inbox/ to inbox/_archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>/.
   - inbox/_failed/ is empty.
9. Regression check: existing dictation pipeline (PTT + `+ Audio file`
   button) still work.

Pass criteria:
- End-to-end latency from 'done speaking' to 'transcript appears' is
  < 90 s (target: ~60 s).
- Transcript is non-empty and sensible.
- source='mobile-inbox' (or equivalent) in DB.
- File correctly archived.
- No regression on existing dictation paths.

If anything goes wrong: use docs/mobile/ios-shortcut.md's
troubleshooting table; the Obsidian sync log (Settings -> Sync ->
Show sync log on either device) is the first diagnostic, per
findings doc Finding 6.

bead), and 3.4 (Iter 3 judge -- this bead runs after the judge passes,
matching the Iter 1 pattern where mb-jbf7 depended on mb-thmd).

live-OS smoke catches regressions judges can't.

Distinct from mb-qxrm (Iter 4 full Wave 5 hardening matrix:
conflict-file injection, machine-fingerprint mismatch, retention
nightly, oversized silent-skip, app-offline catch-up -- all bigger
scope, different bead).

title: ADR 0046 Iter 3 Wave 3.2 courier processor decode ingest archive fail
description:
Wave: 3.2 (ADR 0046 Iter 3). New module src-tauri/src/vault/courier.rs
(or src-tauri/src/inbox/courier.rs paired with Wave 3.1's watcher).

This bead supersedes the original 2026-05-23 sketch description; the new
spec is grounded in docs/spikes/iter3-sync-layer-findings.md.

Responsibilities:
- Consume StableInboxFile events from the channel emitted by Wave 3.1's
  watcher (mb-9lgi).
- Single-in-flight: process one file at a time (Mutex guard or
  single-consumer channel); queue subsequent arrivals.
- Validate:
  - Extension is in allowlist (.m4a / .wav / .mp3) (redundant with
    watcher but defensive).
  - Size > 0 AND size < 50 MB (defensive upper bound; Obsidian Sync
    Standard 5MB cap means oversized won't arrive via sync, but local
    drag-drop into inbox/ could).
  - Log + skip with reason on validation failure.
- Decode: call audio::decode::decode_to_pcm16_mono_16k(path) (Iter 1's
  mb-hxm4).
- Provenance: build IngestProvenance{source: SessionSource::MobileInbox,
  original_filename: file.file_name, received_at_iso: file.observed_at}.
- Ingest: send HeadlessIngestRequest via the crossbeam channel from Iter
  1 ADR §3.2 amendment. Wait for reply (session_id or error).
- On success: move file from inbox/<name> to
  inbox/_archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<name>. Date subdirs prevent collisions
  and aid eventual cleanup. Use std::fs::rename; if it fails (cross-
  device move), fall back to copy+delete.
- On failure: move to inbox/_failed/<name>. Verbose tracing::error!
  with which stage failed (decode? STT? cleanup?). Failed files are NOT
  retried automatically; user can drag them back to inbox/ to re-trigger.
- Emit a SessionsEventBus refresh event after success (Dictations page
  picks up the new row).

Design grounded in:
- Finding 1 (atomic binary delivery) -> the file is guaranteed complete
  by the time the watcher's stability check passes, so this processor
  can read it without further size concerns.
- ADR 0046 §3.2 amendment (Iter 1) -> the HeadlessIngestRequest channel
  is already wired and used by the `+ Audio file` desktop import button.
  The courier is a second producer on the same channel.

Tests via throwaway-crate recipe:
- Mock channel inputs of valid + invalid files; assert correct routing
  (archive vs failed).
- Mock decode failures -> assert file goes to _failed/.
- Mock ingest failures -> assert file goes to _failed/.
- Mock successful ingest -> assert archive move + bus event.

Depends on Wave 3.1 (mb-9lgi) for the input channel. Also depends on
Iter 1's mb-evn3 + mb-hxm4 (both closed).

References:
- Findings: docs/spikes/iter3-sync-layer-findings.md (Finding 1 + Design
  implications / Courier section).
- ADR: docs/adr/0046-mobile-extension-via-vault.md §3.2 amendment.

Status: scoped + grounded; ready to implement (after Wave 3.1).

title: ADR 0046 Iter 3 Wave 3.1 inbox file-watcher with debounce and stability check
description:
Wave: 3.1 (ADR 0046 Iter 3). New module src-tauri/src/vault/inbox_watcher.rs
(or src-tauri/src/inbox/watcher.rs if a top-level inbox/ subsystem makes
more sense; structure choice is implementer's call).

This bead supersedes the original 2026-05-23 sketch description; the new
spec is grounded in docs/spikes/iter3-sync-layer-findings.md (Wave 0 spike
shipped 2026-05-27 + 5 observation rounds run 2026-05-24).

Responsibilities:
- Watch <vault>/inbox/ recursively using the notify crate (or
  notify-debouncer-full if its quiet-window semantics fit). Win11 first,
  macOS later behind the same trait.
- Source-level path exclusions: .obsidian/, .git/, .mockingbird/,
  inbox/_archive/, inbox/_failed/, inbox/_keep/. The .obsidian/ exclusion
  is load-bearing: workspace.json fires every few seconds (Finding 7).
- Source-level filename exclusions: .tmp, .partial, .crdownload, .icloud
  suffixes; ~$ prefix. Defensive insurance against future transports;
  none observed in the spike (Finding 1: binary delivery is atomic, no
  placeholders).
- Extension allowlist for processing: .m4a (primary), .wav, .mp3.
- Debounce: coalesce duplicate FS events within a 100ms window per path
  (Finding 3: every logical change emits 3-4 events within 5-12ms; 100ms
  has comfortable headroom).
- Stability check: when an allowlisted size>0 file is observed, schedule
  a re-check 2 seconds later. Size unchanged at re-check -> stable.
  Size differs -> reset. Two consecutive stable reads required before
  emitting. Even though binary audio arrives atomic (Finding 1), the
  stability check is cheap insurance against future chunked delivery
  AND handles the local-FS drag-drop-half-copied-file edge case.
- Emit StableInboxFile{path, size, observed_at} events to a tokio (or
  crossbeam) channel consumed by the courier processor (mb-txmy / Wave
  3.2). Bounded channel.
- Tracing: info! for file-detected / file-stable, debug! for raw FS
  events.

Tests via throwaway-crate recipe per LESSONS P2 (no whisper-rs / ort /
CUDA deps -> pure-Rust testable):
- Synthetic FS events (mock notify) firing 3-4 duplicates within 10ms ->
  assert exactly one StableInboxFile emitted.
- File growing in size across stability checks -> assert StableInboxFile
  is delayed until two consecutive stable reads.
- Files matching exclusion patterns -> assert no events emitted.
- Files matching allowlist but at 0B -> assert ignored until size > 0.
- File appearing at full size in one event (atomic binary case) -> assert
  StableInboxFile emitted after ~4s (2 stability reads).

References:
- Findings: docs/spikes/iter3-sync-layer-findings.md (Findings 1, 3, 4,
  7 specifically; Design implications section enumerates the watcher
  spec).
- ADR: docs/adr/0046-mobile-extension-via-vault.md §6 combined detector.
- Predecessor spike bead: mb-s8s2 (closed in same commit as findings doc).

Status: scoped + grounded; ready to implement.

title: ADR 0046 Iter 3 Wave 3.3 InboxRuntime wiring and settings-gated lifecycle
description:
Wave: 3.3 (ADR 0046 Iter 3). New module
src-tauri/src/vault/inbox_runtime.rs (paired with Wave 3.1 + 3.2
modules under the same `vault/` subsystem).

Responsibilities:
- InboxRuntime owns: the file watcher thread (Wave 3.1 / mb-9lgi), the
  courier processor thread (Wave 3.2 / mb-txmy), and the channel
  between them.
- Started/stopped based on MobileSyncEnabled + VaultPath settings:
  - On MobileSyncEnabled false-to-true: start runtime (if VaultPath is
    valid and inbox/ exists; create inbox/ if missing).
  - On MobileSyncEnabled true-to-false: stop runtime cleanly.
  - On VaultPath change while enabled: stop + restart with the new
    path.
- Wired in src-tauri/src/lib.rs Tauri setup, parallel to VaultRuntime
  (Iter 2's mb-lvzw). Same lifecycle ownership pattern: one Tauri-
  managed singleton, reacting to typed-settings change events.
- Shares the HeadlessIngestRequest channel sender with the IPC handler
  (Iter 1 + Audio file button uses the same sender) -- this is the
  second producer pattern explicitly authorized by ADR §3.2.
- On Mockingbird startup with MobileSyncEnabled=true: do an INITIAL
  SCAN of inbox/ to pick up any files that arrived while Mockingbird
  was off. Treat as if they just arrived (run through full validation
  + ingest pipeline). This handles "I recorded a memo while my laptop
  was closed" case.
- Tracing logs for: watcher start/stop, file detected, file processed,
  file archived, file failed. Helps Iter 3 smoke debugging
  (mb-... Wave 3.5).

Design grounded in docs/spikes/iter3-sync-layer-findings.md (Findings
1-8 collectively); settings-gated startup mirrors Iter 2's VaultRuntime
for UX consistency: one toggle controls both outbound projection AND
inbound courier.

Tests via throwaway-crate recipe:
- Mock settings changes -> assert runtime starts/stops accordingly.
- Initial scan with pre-existing files in inbox/ -> assert all are
  picked up and processed.
- VaultPath swap while running -> assert clean stop + restart.

Depends on Wave 3.1 (mb-9lgi) + Wave 3.2 (mb-txmy).

title: ADR 0046 Iter 4 setup wizard nested-vault detection and guided migration
description:
Iteration: 4 (polish). Detect and resolve the Obsidian nested-vault trap during Mobile Sync setup. Repro: user creates an Obsidian vault by 'Create new vault' with a name that matches an existing folder; Obsidian silently creates a nested <vault>/<vault>/ structure. Mockingbird then writes to the outer path while Obsidian reads from the inner -- mobile sync appears broken (no files visible in Obsidian) even though everything is working correctly. See LESSONS 2026-05-27 for the full diagnostic walk-through and Dustin's hands-on resolution.

Acceptance: the Mobile Sync setup flow (whether full Iter 4 tab or the existing preview section) detects this case and either: (a) blocks toggle-on until user resolves, with clear instructions, OR (b) offers a one-click auto-migrate that moves .obsidian/ + any root .md files from inner to outer, deletes the empty inner, and continues. Option (b) is the better UX if the file-move is reliable.

Out of scope: detecting non-nested but otherwise-misconfigured vaults (e.g. user pointed Mockingbird at the wrong folder entirely). Just the nested trap.
